title: Constraints & indexes
summary: Inventory per store: one row per (store, sku), never negative, fast lookups by store.
description:
Inventory per store: one row per (store, sku), never negative, fast lookups by store.

Why: Business rules that every writer must respect belong in the database, not only in app code: a composite UNIQUE prevents duplicate stock rows, a CHECK stops negative quantities, and the composite UNIQUE's index (store_id first) also serves 'all items in a store' queries.
objectives: UNIQUE (store_id, sku) — sku alone is NOT unique
store_id indexed (leading column of an index)
CHECK quantity >= 0 (Python/SQL; Prisma has no CHECK — see the lesson)
hints: A composite UNIQUE (store_id, sku) creates an index whose first column is store_id.
The gate tries real INSERTs (rolled back) to prove the rules are enforced.

sql: INSERT INTO lab_inventory (store_id, sku, quantity) VALUES (1, 'A-1', 5), (2, 'A-1', 0)
probes.message: The same SKU in two stores (and a quantity of 0) must be accepted.

sql: INSERT INTO lab_inventory (store_id, sku, quantity) VALUES (1, 'A-1', 5), (1, 'A-1', 3)
probes.message: The same SKU twice in one store must be rejected.

sql: INSERT INTO lab_inventory (store_id, sku, quantity) VALUES (1, 'A-1', -1)
probes.message: A negative quantity must be rejected by a CHECK constraint.

pitfalls: UNIQUE on sku alone — the same SKU can no longer exist in two stores.
Validating quantity only in app code — other writers bypass it.
teachAlong: Cause: rules must hold for every writer.
Effect: constraints + an index in Postgres.
The gate inserts good and bad rows to prove it.
mappingNotes: Compare your code with the Equivalent SQL panel. The gate introspects Postgres and runs rolled-back probe INSERTs.
solution:
from sqlalchemy import String, Integer, Numeric, Boolean, ForeignKey, UniqueConstraint, create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column, relationship


class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

from sqlalchemy import CheckConstraint, Index


class LabStore(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_stores"
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(120))


class LabInventory(Base):
    __tablename__ = "lab_inventory"
    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint("store_id", "sku", name="uq_inventory_store_sku"),
        CheckConstraint("quantity >= 0", name="ck_inventory_quantity"),
    )
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    store_id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(ForeignKey("lab_stores.id"))
    sku: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(32))
    quantity: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer)

engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)
Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
